extracted.intended_audience: laboratory technicians, sanitary inspectors, and bacteriologists performing routine analysis of water and milk
extracted.subtask_description: Laboratory procedures and evaluation criteria for detecting, concentrating, isolating and identifying pathogenic and saprophytic bacteria in water and milk using enrichment and concentration techniques, selective media, culture characteristics, biochemical reactions, and animal inoculation tests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enrichment principle
rubrics_metrics.description: Enrichment, in which the harmless non-pathogenic bacteria may be destroyed or their growth inhibited, whilst the growth of the parasitic bacteria is encouraged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Achieve enrichment by arranging environment (media, incubation temperature, atmosphere) to favor pathogenic organisms at the expense of harmless saprophytes. Example: bile salt broth, anaerobic incubation at 42°C to favour intestinal bacteria and inhibit ordinary water bacteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enrichment method — initial sampling and incubation scheme
rubrics_metrics.description: Number a set of bile salt broth tubes 1–5 (and duplicates 1a–5a) and add specified volumes of water sample: Tube 1 = 0.1 c.c., 2 = 1 c.c., 3 = 2 c.c., 4 = 5 c.c., 5 = 10 c.c.; incubate anaerobically in Buchner's tubes at 42°C.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also prepare double-strength bile salt broth flasks (e.g., 25 and 50 c.c. with corresponding water sample additions) incubated aerobically at 42°C. The bile salt medium plus anaerobic conditions and 42°C selects for intestinal bacteria and inhibits many mesophilic water organisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment of enrichment cultures
rubrics_metrics.description: After 24 hours (and again at 48 if necessary) note: (a) presence/absence of visible growth; (b) reaction of medium as indicated by litmus colour change; (c) presence/absence of gas formation (froth and gas in inner tube).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Replace tubes showing no growth for further incubation. Remove tubes that show visible growth for further microscopic and plating examination regardless of acid/gas presence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plating and colony recognition after enrichment
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare surface plate cultivations upon nutrose agar from each tube showing growth; incubate aerobically 24 hours at 37°C; examine colonies with naked eye or hand lens to recognize colonies of the coli group, typhoid group, paratyphoid group, and streptococci.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From this stage proceed along divergent lines depending on whether bacilli (typhoid/coli) or cocci (streptococci) are suspected. Pick off suspicious colonies and subcultivate on nutrient agar for purification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Isolation and biochemical differentiation of coli-typhoid group
rubrics_metrics.description: After pure culture is obtained, emulsify growth in 5 c.c. sterile saline or broth and use to inoculate a series of media (gelatine streak, agar streak, potato, nutrient broth, litmus milk, and many carbohydrate peptone solutions including dextrose, laevulose, galactose, maltose, lactose, saccharose, raffinose, dulcite, mannite, glycerin, inulin, dextrin peptone solutions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Differentiate isolates into Escherich, Gaertner, and Eberth groups by cultural reactions and biological characters; confirm by agglutination using specific sera. Use results (acid/gas in carbohydrate media, litmus milk reactions, indol, growth characteristics) according to the provided analytical schema and differential table.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analytical scheme for grouping on nutrose agar and subsequent tests
rubrics_metrics.description: Colonies on nutrose agar: red colonies → Escherich group; blue colonies → Gaertner and Eberth groups. Follow-up tests: lactose peptone solution (gas/no gas), glucose peptone solution (acid and gas or not), litmus milk (acid/coagulation/turbidity/serum reaction), indol in bouillon, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the tabulated pattern of acid/gas/indol/litmus milk results and motility/gelatine liquefaction to assign isolates to B. coli communis, B. typhosus, B. paratyphosus, etc. Table-note conventions: + = motile, - = non-motile; C = clot; O = no change; +/- = slight reaction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Numerical interpretation from tube series (most probable presence)
rubrics_metrics.description: If growth of a specific organism is obtained in a series of tubes inoculated with different volumes, calculate the smallest quantity of sample that contains at least one organism. Example: growth in tubes from 4 to 10 (but not 1–3) indicates at least one colon bacillus per 10 c.c. but not per 5 c.c.; presence only in flask No. 7 indicates at least one in every 50 c.c. (20 per litre).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the pattern of positive tubes across the dilution series to estimate the average concentration in the original sample down to the smallest volume tested (e.g., 0.1 c.c.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Concentration method — filtration and resuspension principle
rubrics_metrics.description: Concentrate bacteria from large water volumes by filtering ~2000 c.c. through a sterile porcelain filter candle, then emulsify the bacterial residue on the candle with a measured small volume of sterile bouillon (e.g., 10 c.c.) to produce a concentrated suspension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical equivalence: when 2000 c.c. is concentrated into 10 c.c., 1 c.c. of suspension ≈ 200 c.c. of original water (some organisms may remain in filter pores). Use sterile apparatus (filter candle, Kitasato flask, pump, wash-bottle with sulphuric acid safety valve) and sterilise stoppers and tubing before use. Steps include careful pressure restoration and sterile emulsification with a test-tube brush.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concentration method — tube inocula equivalents for coli-typhoid isolation
rubrics_metrics.description: After concentration, inoculate bile salt broth tubes with measured amounts of the suspension corresponding to specific equivalents of original sample: e.g., 0.05 c.c. suspension = 10 c.c. original, 0.125 c.c. = 25 c.c., 0.25 c.c. = 50 c.c., 0.5 c.c. = 100 c.c., 1.0 c.c. = 200 c.c., 2.5 c.c. = 500 c.c.; also include larger-volume inocula (1, 2, 5 c.c.) added before filtration as required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incubate anaerobically in Buchner's tubes at 42°C and proceed with the same subsequent steps as the enrichment method (inspection, plating, differentiation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative (older) methods and their limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Carbolic method, Parietti's method, Elsner's method, Cambier's candle method are older procedures for isolating coli-typhoid organisms but are described as distinctly inferior to the previously outlined enrichment/concentration methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Carbolic method uses carbolised bouillon incubated aerobically at 37°C and plating on carbolised gelatine incubated at 20°C for several days; Parietti's uses Parietti's bouillon variants; Cambier's depends on organisms passing through porcelain filter into surrounding bouillon. Use these only if necessary, noting their inferiority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Isolation of spore-forming Enteritidis sporogenes
rubrics_metrics.description: Heat 5 c.c. emulsion from the filter candle in a benzole bath at 80°C for 20 minutes to select for spore-bearing organisms; prepare ten tubes of litmus milk and inoculate with measured quantities of the suspension; incubate anaerobically at 37°C.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine after 24 hours for litmus decolourisation or acid, clotting and separation of whey, and gas (fissures/bubbles). Reincubate up to 48 hours if needed. Remove positive tubes, pipette off whey for microscopic exam, and inoculate two guinea-pigs subcutaneously with 0.5 c.c. of whey to observe pathogenic effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Isolation of Vibrio cholerae
rubrics_metrics.description: Inoculate ten tubes of peptone water with measured quantities of suspension; incubate aerobically at 37°C for 24 hours and inspect for delicate pellicle formation indicative of vibrios.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transfer from pellicle to fresh peptone water, test peptone water for indol and nitrite by adding pure concentrated H2SO4, prepare gelatine and agar plates from positive tubes, pick colonies resembling Vibrio cholerae and subcultivate on ordinary media, and confirm by agglutination with serum from an immunised animal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Isolation and confirmation of Bacillus anthracis
rubrics_metrics.description: After emulsifying the filter-candle residue, expose 5 c.c. in benzole bath at 80°C for 20 minutes; inoculate a young white rat subcutaneously with 1 c.c. of the emulsion and observe. Melt nutrient agar, add measured suspension volumes to plates, incubate at 37°C 24–48 hours, pick colonies resembling anthrax, subcultivate, and perform a second animal inoculation with subcultivation to confirm pathogenicity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use full post-mortem examination if the animal succumbs. Animal inoculation is used as a confirmatory pathogenicity test in addition to culture characteristics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Isolation and confirmation of Clostridium tetani (B. tetani)
rubrics_metrics.description: After heat selection as for spore-formers, inoculate three tubes of glucose formate broth with 1 c.c. suspension each and incubate anaerobically at 37°C. From tubes showing growth (with or without gas), inoculate guinea-pigs subcutaneously (0.1 c.c.) and observe; pour agar plates anaerobically and subcultivate suspicious colonies; carry out control cultivations and further inoculation experiments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use anaerobic incubation techniques (Buchner's tubes, Bulloch's apparatus) and animal testing for confirmation if required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creating anaerobic conditions in culture
rubrics_metrics.description: Anaerobic conditions can be obtained by putting cultures up in Buchner's tubes or in Bulloch's apparatus; for litmus milk made with whole milk, the cream layer may suffice to ensure anaerobiosis, or a layer of sterile vaseline/liquid paraffin may be poured over the surface if separated milk is used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appropriate anaerobiosis is essential for selection of intestinal/anaerobic organisms; choose method suitable for medium and material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Milk preservative/adulterant detection tests (qualitative)
rubrics_metrics.description: A set of quick chemical tests to detect common preservatives or treatments in milk: (1) Saul raw milk test: 10 c.c. milk + 1 c.c. 1% ortol + 0.2 c.c. 3% H2O2 → brick red within 30 seconds indicates raw milk; (2) Boric acid test: evaporate, incinerate, treat residue with acid, apply to turmeric paper → rose/cherry-red = borax/boric acid; (3) Formaldehyde (Hehner): 10 c.c. milk + 5 c.c. conc. H2SO4 → violet zone = formaldehyde; (4) Hydrogen peroxide: benzidine + acetic acid → blue coloration = H2O2; (5) Salicylic acid: precipitate caseinogen with acetic acid, filter, add FeCl3 → purple = salicylic acid; (6) Sodium carbonate/bicarbonate: add alcohol and rosolic acid → brownish = pure milk, rose = preserved milk.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these tests to determine whether mixed milk has been pasteurised or preserved; interpret colours within the timeframes given (e.g., Saul test: brick red within 30s for raw milk).

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantitative examination of milk — sampling, dilutions and plating scheme
rubrics_metrics.description: Collect retail mixed milk in sterile bottle packaged in sterile copper case on ice. For quantitative counts prepare four sterile capsules with bouillon dilutions to produce serial dilutions: Capsule I (1 c.c. milk into 9 c.c. bouillon → 1 c.c. = 0.1 c.c. milk), Capsule II–IV follow 10-fold serial 0.1 transfers producing calculated contents. Inoculate numbered gelatine, wort gelatine and agar tubes with specified volumes from sample and dilutions; pour plates and incubate (gelatine at 20°C, agar at 37°C, wort gelatine at 20°C).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific inoculation table: gelatine tubes No.1–12 receive varying volumes (1.0, 0.1 c.c., and dilutions from capsules I–IV as listed). After 24–48 hours inspect and after 48 hours count agar plates for organisms growing at 37°C; after 3–5 days count gelatine plates (20°C) for organisms at 20°C; wort gelatine plates for moulds/yeasts. Note many observers prefer gelatine-agar incubated at 28–30°C for 5 days to estimate total organisms at 28–30°C.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of animal pathogenicity tests for streptococci and other isolates
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine pathogenicity of streptococci by inoculating mice subcutaneously and rabbits intravenously; for other organisms (e.g., anthracis, spore-formers) inoculate appropriate animals (guinea-pigs, rats) with specified volumes of culture or whey and observe for disease, performing post-mortem examination if animals succumb.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Animal inoculation is used as a biological confirmation of pathogenicity in addition to cultural and biochemical identification. Record numerical frequency of pathogenic vs saprophytic isolates as indicated for coli-typhoid groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incubation temperatures and atmosphere selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Select incubation temperature and atmosphere to favour target organisms: 42°C anaerobic for enrichment of intestinal bacteria and to inhibit ordinary water bacteria; 37°C aerobic for subcultures and many identification incubations; 20°C for gelatine plate incubation (for certain colony development); 28–30°C for gelatine-agar when preferred for total counts; 37°C aerobic for Vibrio cholerae isolation (looking for pellicle) and for anthrax cultivation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Temperature selection is a key selective criterion; anaerobiosis (Buchner's tubes, Bulloch's apparatus) and temperature (42°C vs 37°C vs 20°C/28–30°C) are used strategically to select or inhibit particular groups.
